So after 203a5ca7 + e7c1875f land, `moe up` / project-stack daemons still refuse every real dispatch with FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_SEAL_UNCONFIGURED - the reviewer's first sentence persists in deployment. So once 203a5ca7 and e7c1875f land, a `moe up` or project-stack daemon STILL refuses every real dispatch on the fallback port.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 1 — VERIFY-OR-BLOCK GATE (read-only; author no bytes). Record with moe.add_comment. Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it beside every grep, each UNPIPED with its own exit code and a positive control.

THE PREVIOUS PLAN HAD THREE MEASURED FAULTS AND worker-4bba4fa4 AUTHORED ZERO BYTES FINDING THEM. Evidence: comment-0f929a69 and comment-89480f20. All three are corrected below; do not re-derive them.
FAULT 1 — ORDERING. `readCurrentProjectConfiguration` (project-configuration-selection.ts:190-198) takes `(store, input)` and requires an EXACT `{projectId, expectedSettingsDigest}` record, refusing `PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE` otherwise. There is NO discover-current overload. Meanwhile `resolveLaunchEnv` (moe-up-env.ts:67) runs BEFORE store/project selection. So the old plan asked for config authority at a point where no projectId exists yet. Step 3 fixes the ORDER, not the signature.
FAULT 2 — WRONG ALLOWLIST. The old plan checked `ALLOWED_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` in `windows-launch-request.ts` and concluded the two provider keys were absent, so its R6 stop fired deterministically. That is the WRONG roster. The DoD names the right one and it is a COMPOSED SUPERSET: `PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` at `windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:33-43` spreads `...ALLOWED_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS`, `...PROJECT_STACK_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_KEYS`, then MOE_* keys. Extending THAT roster is the mechanism.
FAULT 3 — WRONG TEST PATH. `windows-boundary.test.ts` does not exist. The real consumer is `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts` (its `.ts` and `.js` siblings are there too). Same file family as fault 2, so faults 2 and 3 share one root cause: the old roster named a neighbouring module.

(a) DoD-1 PREREQUISITES — ALL FOUR MEASURED GREEN at HEAD d8552611; re-run each: `git merge-base --is-ancestor a283eb8f HEAD` EXIT 0; task-e7c1875f DONE; task-203a5ca7 DONE; task-05f12b4f (e2e harness authority) DONE.
(b) THE PEER-WIP FENCE IN TASK RAIL 2 HAS EXPIRED: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-context-seal-wiring.ts` prints NOTHING — 203a5ca7's WIP landed and is committed. Re-measure; if anything there is dirty again it is someone's live work and the fence is back.
(c) SIZES, because two rails cap them: `moe-up-env.ts` is 142 lines (room to grow). Task rail 5 says add NOTHING to `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` (at/over the 400 split bound) or `foundation-attempt-service.ts` (397) — re-measure both and route new code into new modules if either would grow.
(d) ADOPT, NEVER DUPLICATE (task rails 1 and 7): the seal wiring, the `launchRequestBody` rewrite, the call-site replacement and the registry-level accepted control belong to task-203a5ca7 and are DONE. Re-measure `git grep -n "context.template" HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/work/` and the seal composition before writing anything — if a mechanism this row needs already landed, verify and compose it rather than re-implementing.
(e) OWNERSHIP: file-field scan across non-DONE rows plus porcelain on every path you will touch.

STEP 2 — RED FIRST, ON THE TWO ROSTERS DoD-2 NAMES. Do not change the ordering yet.

DoD-2 requires that BOTH the daemon env composer AND the Windows project-stack allowlist carry the context-digest key. Write the arms that pin both, and watch them fail.
(1) THE ALLOWLIST ARM, in `windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts` — the REAL consumer (fault 3). Assert `PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` admits the context-digest key. It is a composed roster (`windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:33-43` spreads ALLOWED_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS, the provider credential keys, then the MOE_* list), so assert membership in the COMPOSED set, not in one of its parts — asserting against a part is how fault 2 happened.
(2) THE COMPOSER ARM: assert the daemon's launch env carries the digest key through `resolveLaunchEnv`'s overlay.
(3) THE FAIL-CLOSED NEGATIVE (DoD-4), and it must be GREEN from the start and stay green: with the digest key ABSENT the daemon still boots and still serves every non-Foundation command kind — 203a5ca7's "absent is valid" state — and `unconfiguredFoundationContextSealPort`'s code and layer are UNCHANGED. If this arm ever reds, the change has leaked into the absent-key path, which task rail 4 forbids: no default digest, no "skip the seal" branch, no provider launch without a durable context record committed first.

BEFORE ADDING ANY KEY TO A FROZEN ROSTER, grep its consumers: an exact-count or set-equality assertion on `PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` is a CONSUMER of this change and moves WITH it in the same commit. Name every one you find in the step note; if the roster has a count arm, it changes and that is the assertion working, not a scope breach.

Run standalone, FOREGROUND, UNPIPED: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` and the focused daemon suite. Quote every red with its count line.

STEP 3 — FIX THE ORDERING (FAULT 1). This is the substantive correction and it is a SEQUENCING change, not a signature change.

THE PROBLEM: `resolveLaunchEnv` (moe-up-env.ts:67) runs BEFORE store/project selection, but `readCurrentProjectConfiguration` (project-configuration-selection.ts:190) needs an EXACT `{projectId, expectedSettingsDigest}` and refuses `PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE` without one. Config authority therefore cannot be read at the point the old plan wanted it.

BIND THE CONFIG AUTHORITY AFTER STORE AND PROJECT SELECTION. Sequence: store dependencies -> project selection -> `readCurrentProjectConfiguration` -> the env overlay that carries the digest -> launch. The digest key is added to the launch env only once a project is known, and until then the launch env simply does not carry it — which is the fail-closed absent-key state step 2 arm (3) already pins, not a new branch.

DO NOT ADD A DISCOVER-CURRENT OVERLOAD to `readCurrentProjectConfiguration`. The previous plan assumed one existed; inventing one now would widen a configuration authority's admitted surface to make a sequencing bug easier to live with. If the ordering genuinely cannot be fixed without changing that function's contract, STOP and report — that is a different row and a different review.

DEFERRED FOUNDATION REFUSAL PROVENANCE (named in the re-plan handoff): when the digest is not yet available at composition time, the eventual Foundation refusal must still carry ITS OWN code and layer — `unconfiguredFoundationContextSealPort`'s, unchanged — not a new one invented here and not a generic "not ready". An arm asserts the deferred path's refusal is byte-identical in code and layer to the absent-key path's.

TASK RAIL 5 CAPS: add nothing to `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` (at/over 400) or `foundation-attempt-service.ts` (397). If the sequencing needs code in either, put it in a NEW module with its `.js` bridge and say so in the step note. `moe-up-env.ts` at 142 has room.

Re-run step 2: arms (1) and (2) green, arm (3) still green. Quote the count line.

STEP 4 — EXTEND THE ALLOWLIST AND CARRY THE DIGEST VERBATIM.

Add the context-digest key to `PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` (windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:33-43), in the MOE_* group where its siblings live, and move every consumer assertion step 2 enumerated in the SAME commit. A roster change landing without its count consumers reds the branch for everyone.

TASK RAIL 3 IS ABSOLUTE HERE, and it is the security property this row turns on:
- THE DIGEST IS CARRIED VERBATIM, NEVER RECOMPUTED. The runner receives the value the daemon sealed; it does not derive, re-hash, or validate it into a different value.
- `@moe/runner` GAINS NO `@moe/context` DEPENDENCY. If you find yourself wanting one, you are about to recompute rather than carry — stop.
- NEVER LOOSEN `REQUEST_KEYS` or `snapshotExactRecord` to admit a 15-key body. The exactness is the guarantee; widening it to fit a new field is how caller-shaped data gets in.
An arm asserts the digest the provider receives is byte-identical to the one the daemon composed — compare the two values, both read from production surfaces, never one hand-written.

Re-run `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` and the focused daemon suite: all green, both count lines quoted.

STEP 5 — THE REAL-PROCESS CONTROL (DoD-3). This is the arm that makes the row's title true: the Foundation provider reached WITH ITS SEALED CONTEXT from a PRODUCTION-LAUNCHED daemon.

Extend the foundation e2e harness under task-05f12b4f's authority (that row is DONE — confirm at your HEAD before editing, and adopt its harness rather than building a second one). Run from PowerShell.

Boot the daemon through the PRODUCTION ENTRY: `createStoreDependencies(readStoreDependencyEnv(process.env))` with the composed env from step 3. NOT a fixture daemon, NOT injected ports — the whole point is that the production launch path carries the digest end to end. A control that injects the seal port proves the seal works and proves nothing about the launch path, which is the gap this row exists to close.

THE SEED BUILDER MUST BE PRODUCTION-BACKED (named in the re-plan handoff): whatever seeds the run composes it through production writers, not hand-authored rows. A hand-seeded fixture would let the arm pass against a world no production writer can create.

ASSERT THE PROVIDER ACTUALLY RECEIVED THE SEALED BYTES — not that a launch happened, not that no error was thrown. Capture the provider input and compare its digest to the one the daemon durably recorded. Per task rail 4, no provider launch may occur without a durable context record committed FIRST, so also assert the record exists and precedes the launch.

WINDOWS: close file-backed SQLite handles before any reopen and on every failure path, or the worker dies on a held handle.

STEP 6 — DRILLS, GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE HANDOFF.

RESTORE PROTOCOL: all four production files are TRACKED and were porcelain-clean at plan time, so `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` is a valid restore proof — re-check `git status --porcelain` per path FIRST, since they carry your edits during drills. Any NEW module you added for the rail-5 caps is untracked and needs SHA256 against a `%TEMP%/e4cd1eb6-<workerId>/` backup, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Confirm each mutation LANDED before rerunning; a silent no-op write reads as green. Task rail 6: drills vary ONE degree of freedom and the red arm's TITLE must claim the behaviour that broke.
D1 REMOVE THE KEY from `PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` -> the allowlist arm reds, and the real-process control reds too. Both, because the roster is what lets the digest cross the boundary.
D2 RECOMPUTE THE DIGEST in the runner instead of carrying it verbatim -> the byte-identical arm reds. This is task rail 3's guard and the row's security property.
D3 COMPOSE THE ENV BEFORE PROJECT SELECTION (revert step 3's ordering) -> the composer arm reds with `PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE`. That is fault 1 reproduced deliberately, and it proves the ordering fix is load-bearing rather than incidental.
D4 DEFAULT THE DIGEST when the key is absent -> the fail-closed arm (step 2 arm 3) MUST red. Then default it to a DIFFERENT value -> the SAME arm must red. Absence and a defaulted value are different answers.
D5 LAUNCH WITHOUT THE DURABLE RECORD committed first -> the record-precedes-launch arm reds (task rail 4).
A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report in the row comment, never a pass to bank.

GATES — each alone, FOREGROUND, UNPIPED, with exit code and nonzero `Test Files`/`Tests` lines recorded in a task comment (DoD-5). An exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING.
LEG A: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — quote the `$ tsc` echo.
LEG B: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck`.
LEG C: the focused daemon suite over this row's owned tests.
LEG D: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test`.
LEG E: the real-process control from step 5, run from PowerShell, with its transcript quoted — that is the only leg that bears on DoD-3.
Attribute repo-wide red by path against the merge-base; the delta intersected with this row's owned paths must be EMPTY, foreign red disclosed verbatim and never edited.
LINE CAPS: `wc -l` every production file touched. `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` and `foundation-attempt-service.ts` must be UNCHANGED in line count — if either grew, task rail 5 was breached.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, in the step note: is the digest ever recomputed rather than carried; did `@moe/runner` gain an `@moe/context` dependency (it must not); were `REQUEST_KEYS`/`snapshotExactRecord` loosened (they must not be); does the absent-key path still boot and serve every non-Foundation kind with `unconfiguredFoundationContextSealPort`'s code and layer unchanged; does the real-process control use the production entry rather than injected ports; is the seed builder production-backed; and did any file the rails cap grow.

DURABLE HANDOFF — moe.add_comment, not the completion summary. Keep each under ~4500 chars and SPLIT rather than truncate (both cap at 5000 SILENTLY). Carry step 1's measurements with the freshly-captured HEAD sha; the record that the OLD plan's three faults were ordering, wrong-allowlist and wrong-test-path, and that faults 2 and 3 shared one root cause (a neighbouring module named instead of `windows-project-stack-boundary.*`); the enumerated roster consumers; the five drill outcomes with restore proofs; and every gate leg's exit code and count line including the step-5 transcript. Commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC of this row's owned paths, message BEFORE the `--` (a `-m` after `--` is parsed as a pathspec and nothing lands). Never `git add -A`, never a bare `git commit`.
